ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Given the line $y=kx+b$ passes through the points $A(6,0)$ and $B(2,2)$. According to the graph, write the solution set for the inequality $x-3>kx+b$ with respect to $x$.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a rectangular coordinate system; a descending straight line can be seen passing through the marked point B(2,2) and point A(6,0); beside another ascending straight line is marked y=x-3, and the two straight lines intersect at point C. Reasoning: From the meaning of the problem, it can be known that the descending straight line is y=kx+b. From A(6,0) and B(2,2), calculate its slope k=(0-2)/(6-2)=-1/2. Substitute A(6,0), obtaining 0=(-1/2)·6+b=-3+b, so b=3. Therefore the inequality x-3>kx+b becomes x-3>-x/2+3. Rearranging gives x+x/2>6, namely 3x/2>6, so x>4.
